title: IT Act s. 4 — Legal recognition of electronic records (IT Act s. 4)

content.overview: Legal recognition of electronic records. Section 4 gives legal recognition to information in electronic form so that a legal requirement for information to be written or printed is satisfied where the statutory conditions for accessibility and later reference are met. The analysis must identify the protected record/system, the prohibited act, mental element, statutory condition, evidence and remedy.

content.study:
Statutory rule
Section 4 gives legal recognition to information in electronic form so that a legal requirement for information to be written or printed is satisfied where the statutory conditions for accessibility and later reference are met.

Elements
Identify the object protected by the section, the precise prohibited act, the required knowledge/intent or other mental element and each qualifying condition. Do not convert a technical irregularity into statutory liability without matching the facts to the text.

Evidence
Map source records, system logs, code repositories, contracts, authorisations and communications to the relevant element. Apply BSA 2023 s. 63 where an electronic record is tendered and separately establish attribution and integrity.

Connected provisions
Distinguish legal recognition/admissibility from substantive liability; distinguish compensation under section 43/43A from criminal offences under sections 65 onward. For Government use under section 6, separate statutory recognition from an agency's power or obligation to conduct a transaction electronically.

Current-law caution
Use the provision and rules in force on the relevant date and do not plead struck-down section 66A.

cases.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court reviewed restrictions on online speech under the Information Technology Act.
cases.issue: Whether IT Act s. 66A impermissibly restricted constitutional speech.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 66A was vague and overbroad and violated Article 19(1)(a); it was not saved by Article 19(2).
cases.holding: Section 66A was struck down in its entirety.
cases.relevance: Use only as historical status; do not present s. 66A as a current offence.

cases.name: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
cases.facts: The Court examined the statutory method for proving electronic records.
cases.issue: Whether electronic records can be admitted without the applicable certificate route.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Electronic records must satisfy the special statutory proof requirements applicable to computer outputs.
cases.holding: The Court reaffirmed the certificate discipline for electronic evidence.
cases.relevance: Use with BSA s. 63 and digital-record admissibility.

cases.name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered privacy as a constitutional right in the digital and modern State.
cases.issue: Whether privacy is protected as a Fundamental Right.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Privacy is intrinsic to dignity, liberty and Part III, subject to legality, legitimate aim, proportionality and procedural safeguards.
cases.relevance: Use for surveillance, data protection and informational privacy.

questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether IT Act s. 4 — Legal recognition of electronic records (IT Act s. 4) applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
IT Act s. 4 — Legal recognition of electronic records (IT Act s. 4) is governed by Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles. identify the date, technology, applicable IT Act provision, data regime, intermediary rule and evidence law; distinguish struck-down provisions from current offences.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

I. STATEMENT OF FACTS AND PROCEDURAL PROVENANCE
Set out the material facts, forum, procedural stage, notices, pleadings and documents.

II. STATUTORY AND DOCTRINAL SCHEME
Deconstruct IT Act s. 4 — Legal recognition of electronic records (IT Act s. 4) under Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles, including its purpose, conditions, exceptions and connected provisions.

III. SATISFACTION OF MANDATORY INGREDIENTS
Apply each ingredient to the record, address jurisdiction, limitation, maintainability and the opposing party's strongest objection.

IV. VERIFIED AUTHORITIES
Use the case ratios below only for the propositions they decide and distinguish contrary facts.

V. EVIDENCE AND PRAYER
Address BSA ss. 63, 104 and 109 where relevant, then seek the precise order available from the designated cyber-crime police and criminal court, adjudicating officer, civil court, High Court under Articles 226/227, or competent data-protection and regulatory forum.
